_readme: Maps an abgeordnetenwatch poll topic to the SPECIFIC Lobbyregister field-of-interest
labels that are genuinely on-topic for it. This powers the 'same policy area' tie: a
member holds a role at an org that lists one of these fields, and votes on a poll tagged
with this topic — even though that org never declared lobbying on this exact bill.
This is a WEAKER signal than a declared-Drucksache conflict and must never be presented
the same way (see build-lobby-links.mjs and src/lobby.ts). It only has value if it stays
precise, which means two hard rules when editing this file:
1. Never list a field whose 'de' label is generic ('Allgemeine Energiepolitik', a bare
topic-sector name, etc.) or a '*_OTHER' catch-all ('Sonstiges im Bereich "X"'). Those
are ticked by a huge fraction of all registered orgs regardless of actual relevance —
tested empirically: matching the whole 'Energie' topic against org fields (including
the generic ones) produced 3,171 member/poll pairs, and the first several were
obviously irrelevant (a student-services union and two party economic forums flagged
on a building-energy-retrofit bill). Only list fields specific enough that an org
listing them plausibly has an actual stake — 'Bank- und Finanzwesen', not 'Wirtschaft'.
2. Every field's global frequency across the ~6,900-entry register is noted in a comment
next to it. As a rule of thumb, avoid adding anything above roughly 1,200 (~17% of the
register) — a label that common carries almost no discriminating power.
Topics with no substantive external policy content (e.g. 'Bundestag', which is mostly
MPs' own legal status and parliamentary procedure) are deliberately left unmapped.
3. A TOPIC can be non-discriminating too, not just a field — and then it has to go, however
specific the fields under it are. Two topics were removed for this:
'Politisches Leben, Parteien' listed only its own sector name, so rule 1 removed it.
'Öffentliche Finanzen, Steuern und Abgaben' is the instructive one. It is attached to
16 of 63 current polls (25%) but is the PRIMARY topic of only 4 — the other 12 are
budget-adjacent bills about energy, education or foreign policy that merely move money.
Matching it tied every registered bank to every one of them: Sparkassenverband Bayern
picked up 115 ties, including to the Chancellery's own budget and a BAföG reform.
Deleting its generic self-named field did NOT fix that — the same ties simply came back
under 'Bank- und Finanzwesen', which is a perfectly specific field. The field was never
the problem; the topic was. A bank on a budget bill is not evidence of anything, because
every bill is a budget bill somewhere.
Little is lost: for the 4 genuinely fiscal bills, an org with a real stake will normally
have registered the Drucksache itself — and that declared tie is the stronger signal this
topical tier only ever stood in for.
Format: poll topic string (must match abgeordnetenwatch's field_topics label) -> array of
Lobbyregister field-of-interest 'de' label strings.
